title: Balance of payments entries: the current account and the capital and financial account

stimulus.title: Arland's transactions with the rest of the world
stimulus.text: The table shows entries in the balance of payments of Arland, an invented country, for one year. Positive numbers are money received by Arland residents; negative numbers are money paid by them.

table.caption: Arland's balance of payments entries, billions of dollars (invented data)
rows: Arland residents' purchases of foreign assets

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate Arland's current account balance. Show your work.

rubric.point: Current account balance of -70 billion dollars (a deficit of 70 billion), with the work shown: 240 - 310 + 90 - 60 - 10 - 20
accept: "a deficit of 70 billion dollars" with the work

parts.sample: Current account = exports of goods and services - imports of goods and services + net income + net transfers = (240 + 90) - (310 + 60) + (-10) + (-20) = 330 - 370 - 30 = -70. The current account balance is -70 billion dollars, a deficit of 70 billion dollars.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify Arland's capital and financial account balance, and state whether it is a surplus or a deficit.

rubric.point: Capital and financial account balance of +70 billion dollars, a surplus
accept: the opposite of the current account balance from part (A), stated as a surplus or deficit consistently

parts.sample: The capital and financial account balance is +70 billion dollars, a surplus.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Explain why the current account balance and the capital and financial account balance must sum to zero.

rubric.point: Explains that purchases from abroad beyond what a country earns there must be paid for by selling assets to foreigners or borrowing from them, so a current account deficit is matched by a capital and financial account surplus of the same size
accept: "every transaction is recorded twice: a payment for imports is matched by an asset sold or a debt taken on"
"the current account deficit is financed by a financial inflow"

parts.sample: When Arland buys more goods, services, income and transfers from the rest of the world than it sells, it still has to pay for the difference. It does so by selling Arland assets to foreigners or borrowing from them, which are credits in the capital and financial account. So a current account deficit of 70 is matched by a capital and financial account surplus of 70, and the two balances sum to zero.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Calculate the value of Arland assets bought by foreign residents during the year. Show your work.

rubric.point: 140 billion dollars, with the work: capital and financial account balance = foreign purchases of Arland assets - Arland purchases of foreign assets, so 70 = F - 70 and F = 140
accept: an answer consistent with the balance found in part (B), with the work shown

parts.sample: The capital and financial account balance equals foreign purchases of Arland assets minus Arland residents' purchases of foreign assets: 70 = F - 70, so F = 70 + 70 = 140 billion dollars.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Suppose instead that Arland's exports of services had been 20 billion dollars higher, with every other current account entry unchanged. What would Arland's capital and financial account balance have been?

rubric.point: +50 billion dollars: the current account balance would be -50, so the capital and financial account surplus is 20 billion dollars smaller
accept: an answer 20 billion dollars below the part (B) balance, if part (B) was wrong

parts.sample: The current account balance would be -70 + 20 = -50 billion dollars, so the capital and financial account balance would be +50 billion dollars, a surplus 20 billion dollars smaller than before.
